# S62 — Paired landing route

Serve a real page at `/` for paired devices, so a successful pairing no longer ends on a 404.

**Findings:** G5, U2 · **Size:** S · **Tree:** web

**Not in this slice:** the Today view, mark-made and skip controls, the list link (S22 replaces this page's body and keeps the URL); the PWA manifest (S08).

## Why

`pair_submit` redirects to `/` (`src/larder/web/auth_views.py`, `redirect("/", code=303)`), and the header link in `base.html` points at `/`, but no route serves `/`. A paired device gets the 404 page. Every pairing check from S08 to S21, and an installed icon, ends there until S22 lands.

## Owner input

None. The placeholder wording is "You're paired".

Owner decisions: none needed; run as written, 2026-11-03.

## Implement

1. `planner_db.meal_on(conn, day)`: the `planned_meal` row on that ISO date whose status is `planned`, joined to `recipe.title`; lowest id first; none returns None.
2. `home_views.today(settings)` returns `datetime.now(settings.timezone).date()` (host local time when the timezone is unset). `index()` renders `home.html` with the meal or None.
3. Register the blueprint in `create_app` after `auth_views.init_app`. The endpoint is not in `_OPEN_ENDPOINTS`, so unpaired devices keep getting the 401 page from the existing guard.
4. `home.html` extends `base.html`: a "You're paired" heading, and tonight's title when there is one. No inline script or style.

## Check

- Tests pass; on the dev server, completing a pairing shows the landing page, not the 404 page.
